summary: The Network Information Center announces the weekdays and hours its online system would be available to network users, starting October 4, 1971. Some periods are set aside for development and may be irregular. It also explains what users see after a Telnet connection is made.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC tells network users when the Network Information Center system is expected to be available. It also explains the login details, system messages and support contacts.

questions: when was the nic online system available
subtitle: The Network Information Center publishes its service hours and login instructions.

tldr.problem: Network users needed to know when the NIC system was available and how to access it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC gives a weekday schedule, explains that some hours are irregular, and describes Telnet login information and support contacts.
tldr.outcome: The NIC planned to begin regular service on October 4, 1971, while warning that the schedule was temporary and subject to change.

today: RFC 223 is a NIC service schedule published in September 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Availability Schedule
sections.content:
Regular weekday service was to begin Monday, October 4, 1971. The listed hours were 0500-1200 except Tuesday, when service began at 0800; 1200-1300 unavailable; and 1300-1800 available. Service from 1800-2200 was irregular, and the system was unavailable overnight.

Weekend availability was also irregular. The schedule was temporary, and users in irregular periods could be asked to log off at short notice.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC planned morning and afternoon service on weekdays, with a lunch closure. Evening and weekend access was irregular, and the schedule could change.

sections.title: Telnet Login
sections.content: After a Telnet connection, the NIC system printed a welcome message and then a brief message for network users. To log in, users were to enter their site identifier as the user name, the password ARPA, and an account made from the site identifier and the user's last name.
sections.plainLanguage: Users connected through Telnet and signed in with their site identifier, the listed password and an account combining the site identifier with their last name.

sections.title: Support Contacts
sections.content: The RFC lists Dick Watson for administrative problems, John Melvin for NCP or Telnet problems, and Marily Auerbach or Dirk van Nouhuys for TNLS problems. If NIC staff did not answer, an answering service would take a message for follow-up.
sections.plainLanguage: Different NIC staff handled administrative, connection and TNLS questions. An answering service could take a message if staff were unavailable.
